title: How Attention Shapes a Day
summary: A day is shaped not only by what we do, but by where our attention repeatedly rests.
thesis: Where attention goes, life is lived.
invitation: Follow distraction, choice, and recovery, then leave your own judgment.

groups.title: Distraction often begins before we notice it

items.quote: We often notice distraction long after it begins.
items.context: Distraction is rarely one clear decision; it is a series of tiny turns that went unseen.
items.prompt: Which distraction did you notice latest today?

items.quote: The environment can choose where our next glance goes.
items.context: Notifications, sounds, and easy entrances compete for the next moment of attention before thought begins.
items.prompt: What most often chooses your next step for you?

groups.title: Focus is not tension; it is returning
groups.description: Understand focus as the ability to recover.

items.quote: Noticing the drift is already part of returning.
items.context: Focused people are not free from distraction; they notice it earlier and blame themselves less.
items.prompt: What kind of reminder helps you return?

items.quote: What matters must be chosen repeatedly.
items.context: A long-term direction does not automatically occupy a day; it must regain its place in many concrete moments.
items.prompt: What is worth choosing once more today?
